title: ECS clusters
idea: An Amazon ECS cluster is a named group where your tasks and services run. It supplies the compute capacity they run on.
points: A task is one running copy of your containers, started from a task definition.
A service keeps a set of tasks running in a cluster.
Capacity is compute that runs tasks, such as Fargate, EC2, or ECS Managed Instances.
Clusters are separate per Region, and one cluster can mix capacity types.

hero.title: Fargate or EC2 capacity

left.title: Fargate: AWS runs the servers
items: You set CPU and memory for each task.
No instance types to choose and no servers to scale.
Each task runs isolated from other tasks.
Suits getting started and variable workloads.

right.title: EC2: you run the servers
items: You choose the instance types (virtual server sizes) and how many.
You maintain the instances and manage their capacity.
Tasks run on instances registered to the cluster.
Fits specific instance types or custom machine images.

hero.verdict: A cluster can mix both kinds of capacity; pick per workload.

code.title: Create a cluster
code.caption: The smallest cluster is a name in one Region. Replace `<cluster>` and `<region>`.

walk.text: Create a cluster. Without `--cluster-name`, ECS creates one named `default`.
Describe it. `status` reads `ACTIVE` once ready; `runningTasksCount` and `activeServicesCount` start at 0.

code.title: Add Fargate capacity
code.caption: A cluster created with Fargate attached as its capacity and as the default.

walk.text: Attach the `FARGATE` capacity provider, the named source of Fargate capacity.
Make it the default for tasks and services that name no other capacity.

pitfalls: Check the Region before you create or look for a cluster; clusters never cross Regions.
Pick EC2 capacity only if you will maintain the instances and their capacity.
Fargate Spot is cheaper, but AWS can interrupt tasks; use it only for restart-tolerant work.

quiz.q: With plain EC2 capacity, who chooses the instance types and maintains the instances?
quiz.why: EC2 capacity is the full-control option: you choose and maintain the instances. With Fargate, AWS runs the servers.

takeaway: A cluster is where tasks run; its capacity decides who runs the servers.
